speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the skin lesions and tell me exactly where your wrist pain is located?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent trip to Minnesota and the migratory joint pain, did you notice any expanding red rash or a tick bite on your skin during or after the camping trip? I also need to know if you have experienced any headaches, fatigue, or facial swelling.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: The violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on your hands and wrists, combined with acute arthritis and your recent camping trip, are highly suggestive of meningococcemia. REQUEST TEST: Blood_Culture, Lumbar_Puncture.
